ruleName: Movable Obstructions; Replacing Ball on Spot
title: Ball Moves When Removing a Movable Obstruction in a Bunker
question: Your ball comes to rest against a rake lying in a bunker. Before playing, you carefully lift the rake away. As you do, the ball rolls a few inches down the slope. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: Play the ball from its new position because it moved naturally.
Replace the ball on its original spot with no penalty.
Replace the ball and add a one-stroke penalty.
The ball is unplayable and must be dropped under penalty.

explanation: A bunker rake is a movable obstruction, which you are allowed to remove at any time. If the ball moves as a result of removing the rake, there is no penalty. You must simply replace the ball on its original spot before playing. If the ball will not stay at rest on its original spot, it must be placed on the nearest spot where it will remain at rest, no nearer the hole and still in the bunker. (Rule 15.2a(1), Rule 14.2e)
